scope: Characterize quest opcodes in the 1.23b client. Goal stated as 'QuestProgress, QuestAccept, QuestComplete, QuestObjective, etc.'. Reframing: in 1.x there is NO dedicated 'Quest*' packet family. Quest state flows through the existing Event/Director/GenericData wire layer plus a single dedicated client receiver (JobQuestCompleteTriple s2c 0x01A2). All gameplay-side semantics live in Lua scripts subclassing QuestBase / QuestDirectorBaseClass. This manifest catalogs (a) the wire opcodes that carry quest traffic, (b) the QuestBase / QuestDirectorBaseClass C++ scaffolding and its slot map, (c) the dedicated JobQuestCompleteTriple receiver, and (d) the Lua-callback firers tied to quest lifecycle.

key_reframing: There is no QuestProgress, QuestAccept, QuestComplete, or QuestObjective wire opcode in 1.23b.

Quest state in 1.x is driven by SERVER-side scripts using the Event/Director state machine. The client side runs Lua-script subclasses of QuestBase / DirectorBase / QuestDirectorBaseClass; all customization-per-quest lives in those scripts, not in dedicated wire packets.

The wire surface for quests is multiplexed across the Event family (0x012D..0x0131, 0x0136, 0x016B), GenericData (0x0133), GAM property sync (0x0137 SetActorProperty + 0x017A SynchGroupWorkValues), and the SendLog gameMessage family (0x0157..0x016A, including 0x0167 which is the most-emitted quest-related system message). One dedicated receiver opcode exists: 0x01A2 JobQuestCompleteTriple - and it only fires the 'completion celebration' UI for class-quest completions that don't involve NPC interaction.

Quest discovery in symbols.json is therefore a polyglot inventory rather than a packet-family characterization: it cuts across LuaActorImpl slot 78 (Pattern C receiver), Control::MyPlayer slots 4+5 (Lua firers), Control::CharaBase slot 5 (_onFinalize chain), the SendDataPacket('qtdata',...) -> GenericDataPacket plumbing, and the master Lua-class instantiation dispatcher FUN_0075f9b0.

Three Lua-side concepts are load-bearing: (a) DirectorBaseClass.delegateEvent (server invokes named method on client-side director/quest via RunEventFunction 0x0130 + matching client-side method dispatch); (b) directorWork._save / _temp / _sync work-tables (server pushes state via SyncWriter -> SetActorProperty / SynchGroupWorkValues); (c) QuestBase slot 28 = FUN_006dcfd0 (likely getQuestData, the canonical 1.x Lua-side accessor cited in archived community-chat notes).

key_findings: No QuestProgress / QuestAccept / QuestComplete / QuestObjective wire opcode exists in 1.23b. Quest state is multiplexed across the Event/Director family (0x012D, 0x012E, 0x012F, 0x0130, 0x0131, 0x0136, 0x016B), GenericData (0x0133), GAM property sync (0x0137 / 0x017A), SendLog gameMessage (0x0167 most prominent), and the single dedicated Quest receiver (0x01A2 JobQuestCompleteTriple).

0x01A2 JobQuestCompleteTriple is the ONLY dedicated quest opcode in the binary. It is 6-slot Pattern C receiver with a fully-decompiled chain (LuaActorImpl slot 78 -> ctor -> 2-step gated dispatcher FUN_00785BF0 -> slot 5 -> FUN_006F9520 JobQuestObject swapper at MyPlayer+0x110).

QuestBase is a 34-slot multi-inheritance C++ class at vtable RVA 0xbdfddc + secondary RTTI marker at 0xbdfdd0. sizeof = 0x64. Slot 1 is the universal Lua New() factory FUN_00777030; slot 28 (FUN_006dcfd0) is the Quest-specific Lua hook (likely getQuestData). NO BCS-Y entries for ANY QuestBase artifact

All concrete Director/Quest types (OpeningDirector, ZoneDirector, WeatherDirector, GuildleveDirector, HarvestDirector, CraftDirector, QuestDirectorMan0g001..030, SimpleQuestBattle subclasses, Guildleve subclasses, etc.) live ONLY as Lua scripts subclassing DirectorBase / QuestDirectorBaseClass / SimpleQuestBattleBaseClass / GuildleveBaseClass. RTTI scan returns zero matches for any of these names - the C++ binary only has the base classes.

The 'qtdata' / 'qtmap' RPC pattern (RequestQuestJournalCommand.lua + Player.SendDataPacket) rides on GenericDataPacket (s2c 0x0133). UserDataReceiver dispatches through LuaActorImpl slot 59 and its primary two-slot vtable (Pattern A); its secondary six-slot vtable is an MI scaffold, not Pattern C.

Server-driven quest behavior runs through DirectorBaseClass:delegateEvent which wire-rides on s2c 0x0130 RunEventFunctionPacket. delegateEvent invokes a NAMED method (processEventXxx, processTtrXxx, onTalk, onPush, onNotice, onKillBNpc, onNpcLs, onUpdate) on the client-side director or quest Lua instance. All per-quest customization is server-side and routed through this single opcode.

Two LuaActorImpl::vftable slots are tied to JobQuest lifecycle: slot 78 (FUN_0076C690) = JobQuestCompleteTriple receiver wrapper (Pattern C dispatch); MyPlayer::vftable slot 4 (FUN_0070A350) = _onJobQuestCompleteFirst/Second/Third fire; MyPlayer::vftable slot 5 (FUN_00706A50) = _onCancelJobQuestCompleteFirst/Second/Third + _onFinalize fire.

The MyPlayer+0x110 storage location for the 36-byte JobQuestObject (3 x 12B entries = 'last 3 completed job quests') is a CONFIRMED per-player state field. Server pushes new entries via 0x01A2; client side reads via Lua. No existing struct entry in structs.json for JobQuestObject layout.
The 14 function candidates are not present in symbols.json. The proposed BCS-Y-0535..0549 identifiers in this manifest are noncanonical; symbols.json owns allocation.
JobQuestCompleteTripleReceiver and its two-step dispatcher FUN_00785BF0 use Pattern C. UserDataReceiver does not: LuaActorImpl slot 59 reaches primary slot 1 FUN_008A0190 through Pattern A.

Lua-side surface for quests in lua_api_index.json: 17 names match quest/leve/journal/guildleve. Five are _on* fires (_onJobQuestCompleteFirst/Second/Third, _onCancelJobQuestComplete*). One is the C++ N-API method _cancelJobQuestCompleteTriple. Three are accessor APIs (_getQuestActorForCutSceneReplay, _isCompletedCutSceneReplayQuest, _deleteQuestActorForPreview).
open_questions: Is QuestBase slot 28 (FUN_006dcfd0 -> tail-jmp via FUN_00cc7170 -> +0x13f69) actually getQuestData? archived community-chat notes. Confirming requires following the JMP target +0x13f69 from 0x00cc7170 (resolves to 0x00ce0ad9 ish, needs lookup) and reading the body for the get-named-field pattern. Worth a focused decomp.

Where do server-side AddQuest / CompleteQuest / RemoveQuest commands actually surface on the wire?...); _0x02Packet (s2c 0x0002; 48 bytes). 0x0002 is NOT in the pcap quest captures; either 0x0002 is consumed before reaching the captured stream Worth checking the 0x0002 dispatcher.

0x0133 GenericDataPacket in quest captures has payload 224 bytes consistently. The 'qtdata' RequestQuestJournalCommand emits a variadic LuaParam list - 224 bytes is the marshalled payload after the param-pack serializer. Decoding the 224-byte shape would expose the qtdata / qtmap variant tags and the per-quest journal fields.

Three Lua-side quest journal callback names; processTtrNomal003; etc.) are dispatched; 0x0130 RunEventFunctionPacket; the per-name decode of which method on which director is purely a server-side construction. Symbolically attributing 'this RunEventFunction call drives method X' from a pcap requires payload disassembly of the 176-byte 0x0130 frame.

Pattern C gate 1 byte DAT_012C41AF is shared with KickReceiver - is it a global 'last receiver result' or is it owned by a specific subsystem and shared opportunistically? Gate 2 DAT_012C3120 has zero documented users besides Pattern C dispatcher - finding write sites would name its subsystem.

The master Lua-class dispatcher FUN_0075F9B0 (7,481 B, 79 class-name PUSH-immediates) is uncataloged. Tracing its per-name routing would correlate each Lua class name with its slot-1 factory address, including the known QuestBaseClass -> FUN_00777030 edge and 78 other entries.

Is 0x00E3 SetActorQuestGraphicPacket actually the only graphic-marker opcode for quests, or are there sibling opcodes in the actor cluster 0xCC..0xE5 that also carry quest visual state? The actor cluster dispatch model's generic-actor-vftable[9] dispatch makes them invisible to receiver maps.

Quest abandonment is NOT in the pcap corpus (per the xivl-captures capture catalog). The c2s opcode for player-initiated quest abandon is therefore unknown from corpus evidence - it likely flows through EventUpdate 0x012E with a specific selector byte but the exact selector is undecoded.

This survey found ZERO existing BCS-Y entries for the QuestBase scaffolding; ZERO for DirectorBase This is a systematic catalog gap Worth a meta-discussion on how doc-derived knowledge should be promoted.
